html:
SMTO-TSK-0024 — A queued task's saved settings don't match

GUID: 6a1c5c1c-505b-4635-9d76-c88724fe067d
Slug: queue-snapshot-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • When you queue a task, SMTO saves its settings so it runs as you asked. This task's saved settings are incomplete or no longer match, so SMTO didn't start it. An earlier copy may already have started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page and look in the conversation for a reply to this task, without clicking anything else. The task may already have started from an earlier attempt, and adding it again would do the work twice.
  2. If it hasn't started, open the Queued list above the message box and select Delete queued task for this item. The saved copy of its settings can't be trusted, so it shouldn't run as it is.
  3. Check your model and behavior settings in the message box, then type the request again and send or queue it. A new queued task saves a fresh, complete copy of your current settings.

What success looks like

  • The new task appears in the Queued list or starts, and runs once with the settings you chose.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; mention if this queue item was created before SMTO was updated.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A queued request was refused because its captured execution snapshot is incomplete or unprepared, its snapshot digest does not match, or its behavior/summarize settings differ from the prepared request (including legacy queue items that cannot be verified).

What this means

  • Queued submission lacks required captured fields/prepared state, fails its digest, or disagrees with immutable model, behavior or other accepted snapshot choices. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Queued submission lacks required captured fields/prepared state, fails its digest, or disagrees with immutable model, behavior or other accepted snapshot choices.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the complete captured envelope, digest and prepared request before deciding whether a new queue item is needed.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the queue_submissions row and prepared request for this queue item: required snapshot fields, snapshot_digest, behavior effort and summarize settings must match the prepared request. Check whether the original submission was already claimed or produced a run before doing anything; then prepare a new queue item with the intended settings instead of substituting settings into the existing prepared request.
  • Reopen the queue item and verify its captured selections. Prepare a new queue item for changed settings after checking whether the original request was submitted; do not substitute settings in an existing prepared request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original submission is reconciled and any accepted item retains one consistent immutable snapshot.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
